transcript.text: At the same time, USFS Ranger David Fuller receives the alert on his tablet and begins driving to the nearest access point.
The Fire Responder AI System shows him the best route to get there.
On route, the drone creates a communications link to the ground station at Eagle County Airport.
This network will become the local tactical network used by all parties for the common operating picture.
The drone AI begins evaluating threats, escape routes, safety zones, and ingress egress vulnerabilities for ground assets.
This information is uploaded to the Denver Dispat Center and incorporated into the comp virtual space.
At the Dispat Center, incident commander Maria Rodriguez monitors the emerging situation.
The Denver AI merges the drone's live data of the fire spread and displays on Maria's monitor its predicted advance of a steep gulch filled with the dead standing temporary.
She accesses a resource dashboard.
The AI also displays all available resources.
Three Type 1 helicopters at nearby bases.
Two air tankers working a Wyoming fire but available for diversion and four hotshot crews within two hours drive time.
Maria recognizes the need for air support and assigns an air tactical group supervisor or ATGS to coordinate flights into the fire zone.
She selects the air resources and the AI notifies them to launch.
The ATGS arrives on scene and begins orbiting the fire.
Their workstation automatically joins the network and exchanges information with the incident commander and ground teams.
On the ATGS workstation is a list of incoming assets, their status and ETA.
Flight paths to targets, drop points, and locations of nearby ground teams are then sent to the air tankers where the pilots can see the information in their head up display.
Drones and AI technology trained in wildland firefighting can monitor many data streams and flag increasing risk indicators.
These decision support tools can help wildland firefighters make safe effective decisions quickly.
Drones and AI utilizing a local tactical network can share this information to the entire response team.
The ATGS coordinating with the IC and ground teams can designate drop points which are shared in the COP.
This future concept of operations can become reality, with NASA's advanced capabilities for emergency response operations projects.
